reading_rule: Consume each row as a premise or falsifier before proof search. A result implied by a row is dominated; use the stronger row and continue toward the unrestricted parent theorem. Route choice remains unrestricted.

results.exact_statement: A closed length-at-most-two connector theorem on the dense generic normalized locus extends to every normalized polynomial; radial shrinking then gives strict length and strict containment for the open theorem.
results.hypotheses: Monic normalized polynomial; the generic closed theorem is proved on the dense simple/generic locus; lower semicontinuity of the connector functional.
supersedes: separate equality, degeneration, radial strictification, and compactness repairs attached to each local connector
results.why_it_matters: It removes equality, degeneration, and strictification from every local bridge attack; proving the closed generic connector is enough.

results.exact_statement: If a connected carrier in {|P| <= 1} contains at least two roots and is intrinsically covered within distance 1 by one root, compactness/visibility overlap yields two roots joined inside {|P| <= 1} with length <= 2.
results.hypotheses: A connected compact carrier, at least two roots on it, and root-to-every-point intrinsic distance at most one from a single covering root.
supersedes: reproof of the final path-concatenation and visibility-overlap consumer after a radius-one intrinsic cover is found
results.why_it_matters: COVER is already a complete parent consumer; packets must construct the missing cover rather than reprove path concatenation.

results.exact_statement: The full-energy-charged lifetime aggregate and the strict critical budget are available in stronger joint form; the remaining defect is selection/attachment compatibility, not scalar budget.
results.hypotheses: Regularized critical-value/merge-tree setting and the source theorem's active-component bookkeeping.
supersedes: weaker scalar sum, product, or first-critical energy budgets that do not select an attachment-compatible object
results.why_it_matters: It bans returning a weaker sum or product inequality and locates the actual bridge at a same-object attachment selection.

results.exact_statement: On a tied Newton-face fibre, the complete signed moment hierarchy and exact product identity hold for the full inverse-sheet block; inverse-sheet product bounds alone are dominated by this theorem.
results.hypotheses: A regular tied Newton-face fibre with the full algebraic inverse-sheet block and multiplicities counted as in the source theorem.
supersedes: inverse-sheet product bounds that discard the signed moment hierarchy or split the full fibre block
results.why_it_matters: Any inverse-sheet attack must preserve the full block and spend the hierarchy through monodromy/attachment, not headline its weaker product corollary.

results.exact_statement: The weighted attachment-tree selector is sharp and the transport loss is exactly the common-ancestry factor; the unresolved theorem is polynomial-specific compensation of that factor on the same selected object.
results.hypotheses: Root-indexed attachment tree with the landed entrance-energy identities and nonnegative node weights.
supersedes: abstract average selectors that ignore the exact common-ancestry transport loss
results.why_it_matters: It isolates the exact topology/metric compatibility factor and forbids pretending an abstract average already selects an attached polynomial pair.

results.exact_statement: For a proper root cluster S of size k, the conditional induction certificate rho_S^k max_{z in conv(S)} |r_S(z)| <= 1 suffices; it is strictly sharper than multiplying separately attained per-factor maxima.
results.hypotheses: The closed degree-k theorem, a proper cluster S, rho_S its minimum-enclosing-disc radius, and the displayed common-path envelope inequality.
supersedes: products of independently attained per-factor maxima on a proper root cluster
results.why_it_matters: This is the only genuinely stronger survivor from the four returns and creates a new target-sufficient selector route without weakening the corpus.

results.exact_statement: A Jordan contour enclosing exactly one connected critical-edge subtree has one full cycle on the incident sheet block and fixes the complement; an average complete-lift length at most two on that moved block is target-sufficient.
results.hypotheses: Generic ray-separated component, connected critical-edge subtree, and an isolating Jordan value domain inside the unit value disk.
supersedes: full-fibre metric budgets that retain fixed sheets or inadmissible critical values
results.why_it_matters: It removes inadmissible critical values and fixed sheets from the metric budget; topology is occupied and only the integrated geometric cost remains.

results.exact_statement: For a degree-d branched preimage component W and access arc alpha, the sum of all moved lollipop lift lengths is exactly 2 Lambda(alpha,W)+length(boundary W).
results.hypotheses: A regular Jordan value boundary, one Jordan preimage component W, and a critical-value-free access arc from the zero fibre.
supersedes: opaque fixed-block average-length bounds that do not expose access length and preimage perimeter separately
results.why_it_matters: It turns the opaque fixed-block average into the exact geometric inequality 2 Lambda+perimeter<2d and creates a direct route plus a complementary Bergman route.

results.exact_statement: For an isolated simple critical point c, the mean length of the two complete lifts of a shrinking singleton critical-value lollipop converges to the total canonical inverse-ray arm length L(c).
results.hypotheses: A simple critical point c with nonzero critical value distinct from all other critical values and lying in the open unit value disk.
supersedes: treating singleton critical-ray selection and shrinking-cluster monodromy as unrelated proof routes
results.why_it_matters: It identifies the combined-charge critical-ray selector as the singleton limit of the exact cluster budget, making these routes one proof throat. A proof that some admissible c has L(c)<2 immediately yields a strict singleton-cluster certificate.

results.exact_statement: The target-sufficient admissible product is exactly product_v h_v, where h_v=(L(v)/2)/r_v^((k_v-1)/n). The Bergman-Polya certificate proves h_v<=1 on an explicit bulk cherry region. Universal per-cherry and per-rooted-subtree inequalities are stronger than the parent requires: an uncertified cherry with an admissible parent can remain open as multiplicative debt in its ancestor block. All 126 corpus misses and 178/180 stress misses are internal in this sense; only a miss whose parent is the virtual level-one cut is a genuine standalone base. The corpus has zero such terminal misses and stress has two, with largest sampled factor 0.853771268558. A deterministic cubic also falsifies naive independent substitution of each certified cherry's standalone sqrt(B_v) majorant: the actual subtree product is 0.839217266469 but the hybrid bound is 1.075474341153. The exact open throat is therefore parent-coupled area/capacity or another adaptive open-block closure that retains certified-child slack, with only virtual-cut misses treated separately.
results.hypotheses: Simple generic critical points, canonical descending inverse-ray edge lengths, and the admissible set A={c:|f(c)|<1}.
supersedes: universal per-cherry, per-node, or per-rooted-subtree inequalities stronger than the exact global admissible-product obligation
independent multiplication of standalone Bergman-Polya cherry majorants inside a parent subtree
results.why_it_matters: It removes both the certified cherry region and the unnecessary universal-cherry obligation, while the hybrid cubic prevents throwing away the certified child's parent-compatible slack. Internal near-ties are grafting debt, not a second independent base problem; the proof should couple child area/capacity to its parent or close adaptive open blocks by another global mechanism.

results.exact_statement: A single grouped critical-value lollipop proves Erdős 1041 on an open coefficient neighbourhood of every strict regular polygon in every degree, with exact model length 2(r-s)+(2 pi/n)s.
results.hypotheses: A sufficiently small coefficient neighbourhood of z^n-r^n with 0<r<1 and the grouped critical-value contour retained inside the unit value disk.
supersedes: rederivation of a local connector near strict regular polygons without a quantitative hard-regime transfer
results.why_it_matters: It supplies the exact local endpoint mechanism; the remaining hard-regime splice is quantitative cluster control rather than a new local connector.

results.exact_statement: A monic cubic with exact Gaussian-rational data refutes the proposed pointwise first-critical pair-energy cone for all sufficiently small positive perturbations.
results.hypotheses: The explicit cubic family and the precise pair-energy inequality (PEC) in the source.
supersedes: the pointwise first-critical pair-energy cone and perturbative repairs that preserve the same false selector
results.why_it_matters: Pointwise first-critical energy selection is closed; only aggregate or differently coupled substitutes may launch.

results.exact_statement: An exact quartic refutes the fixed-nearest-pair critical-energy geometric-mean selector within the admissible polynomial class.
results.hypotheses: The explicit quartic, its exact critical ordering, and the fixed-pair CE-GM claim stated in the source.
results.why_it_matters: The pair must be adaptive and attachment-compatible; a fixed nearest pair cannot be revived as the missing selector.

results.exact_statement: The tied-face full-block pointwise L1 bound is false even though the exact moment and product identities remain true.
results.hypotheses: The tied Newton-face block and the pointwise L1 inequality isolated in the source countermodel.
supersedes: the tied-face full-block pointwise L1 shortcut
results.why_it_matters: The fixed-block attack must exploit cancellation, variation, or monodromy rather than the refuted pointwise L1 shortcut.

results.exact_statement: The abstract charged-lifetime scalar allocation does not force the required compatible pair; polynomial-specific structure is indispensable.
results.hypotheses: The finite weighted-tree abstraction and scalar allocation assumptions in the source theorem.
supersedes: purely scalar charged-lifetime allocation detached from polynomial attachment topology
results.why_it_matters: A scalar budget detached from topology cannot close the theorem; charge and attachment must live on the same component/pair.

results.exact_statement: The exact tied-face two-spoke and sextic origin-spoke witnesses rule out a universal fixed straight-spoke pair construction.
results.hypotheses: The explicit tied-face/sextic polynomial witnesses and straight-spoke containment claims in the sources.
supersedes: universal fixed straight two-spoke or origin-spoke connector constructions
results.why_it_matters: Curved, intrinsic, adaptive carriers remain open; fixed straight arms do not.

results.exact_statement: Separately resolving and circling every radial critical slit has full-cycle monodromy but double-charges the critical tree and exceeds the average length-two budget on open cubic and quartic charts.
results.hypotheses: The canonical thin separate-slit lollipop on a generic ray-separated degree-k component.
supersedes: separate-slit contours that circle every critical value independently and double-charge the critical tree
results.why_it_matters: Monodromy topology alone is insufficient; admissible critical values must be grouped and the integrated perimeter/access cost must be controlled.
